children: MUFG Bank maintains its bias for further weakness in Indonesian rupiah against the dollar, according to a research report. "Indonesia remains one of our key concerns," senior currency analyst Lloyd Chan says. "Our existing framework points to a combination of higher U.S. yields, weaker external balances from elevated oil prices and a tougher trade-off for Bank Indonesia," Chan says. MSCI-related worries add "another layer of pressure" on the rupiah, the analyst says. "MSCI has launched a consultation to potentially reclassify Indonesia directly from Emerging Market to Standalone Market status," Chan notes. MUFG Bank currently forecasts the dollar at 18,350 rupiah in 4Q 2026 and 18,500 in 1Q 2027. The dollar is 0.2% lower at 18,020.50 rupiah, according to FactSet data. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
